findings: The market already prices AI supply in the top ratings. AA spreads rose from 0.47 to 0.58 of BBB spreads in a year, and the A-minus-AA gap fell from 18bp to 10bp. That ratio is the axis for the supply question. It rises to about 0.64 if supply grinds on and falls to about 0.46 if capex is cut.

A capex cut splits credit in two. It helps the bonds of the large AI spenders, because they borrow less. It hurts everyone who lent against the build-out: HY technology, HY power producers, HY real estate and non-bank lenders.
Today's spreads are fair only if calm is about twice as likely as judged here. IG at 94bp needs a 58% weight on 'Supply absorbed', against 28% here.

Most of the expected widening comes from two tail scenarios. Hard landing and funding accident carry 17% of the probability and about three quarters of the expected IG move. The two most likely scenarios move IG by -12bp to +14bp.
IG income covers only 7bp of widening over six months. Four of the five scenarios exceed that. HY income covers 57bp before default losses.
This agrees with the two Willer and Saunders rules checked on 22 Nov 2026. The volatility rule and the lending-standards rule both say not to hold credit spread risk.
limits: Every probability and spread move is judgement. The script checks coherence, not correctness.
Free data has no sector spread levels. Sector rows are changes from today, and the weights are rough index shares.
Spread durations of 6.6 years for IG and 3.1 years for HY are assumptions, not index data.
Carry cover ignores default losses. For HY the true cushion is smaller.
The fair-value weights assume today's spread equals the expected future spread. That ignores the risk premium.
Several news facts rest on one source each. Examples are the construction-loan force majeure and the 20bp tech premium.
calibration: April 2025 peak: IG 121bp, HY 461bp (FRED). Used as the size of a growth scare without recession.
One-year range to 19 Nov 2026: IG 73 to 94bp, HY 260 to 352bp (FRED). Used for the calm scenario.
Willer and Saunders ch03 Table 3.5: median recession widening of 124bp for IG and about 785bp for HY. Used to cap the accident scenario.
2022 hiking-cycle peaks near IG 165bp and HY 600bp. From memory, not checked against data.

spine.name: Supply absorbed
spine.test: Otherwise. Capex holds, growth holds, and the Fed stops at 4.25% or lower.

observables.threshold: 4.25 or lower on 2027-05-22, and no earlier test is true

evidence: Oil fell from $110 to $90 in a month and 10-year breakeven inflation is at a three-year low of 2.15% (FRED DCOILWTICO, T10YIE).
The October SLOOS is near neutral at 1.7% net tightening (FRED DRTSCILM).

spine.name: Higher rates, supply grind
spine.test: Fourth. The Fed funds upper bound is 4.50% or higher on the horizon date.

observables.series: AA to BBB spread ratio (FRED BAMLC0A2CAA / BAMLC0A4CBBB)

evidence: Futures price a December hike at about 95%. The October minutes say almost all participants favour further hikes (CNBC, 18 Nov 2026).
The 2-year Treasury yields 4.76% against a 4.00% policy ceiling (FRED DGS2, DFEDTARU).
Goldman forecasts $420bn of hyperscaler IG issuance in 2027. SanCap forecasts up to $450bn.

spine.name: AI digestion
spine.test: Third. The five largest AI spenders guide combined 2027 capex to $900bn or less, or two of the five cut guidance.

observables.series: Fourth-quarter earnings guidance, late January to early February 2027
observables.threshold: combined 2027 capex of $900bn or less, against a consensus above $1,000bn

evidence: Nvidia lost about half its market value in six weeks. Reuters reported an SEC accounting probe on 20 Nov 2026.
Tech IG borrowing costs are the highest since 2009 by one report. The 2027 funding gap is put at about $291bn (SanCap, 20 Nov 2026).
Against: strong Nvidia earnings in November show demand had not yet dropped.

spine.name: Hard landing
spine.test: Second. The manufacturing ISM prints under 50 for two months in a row, or the Sahm rule reaches 0.50.
evidence: Against: the October ISM is 55.5 and rising, after ten months of expansion.
For: the Fed is hiking into an equity fall of 8% on the S&P 500 and 13% on the Nasdaq.

spine.name: Funding accident
spine.test: First. A bank or insurer with over $50bn of assets fails or is rescued, or the Fed opens an emergency facility, or the IG primary market shuts for five business days.

observables.threshold: five straight business days with no deals, outside holidays

evidence: CCC spreads are at a three-year high of 1361bp (FRED BAMLH0A3HYC). CoreWeave bonds yield about 16% (CNBC, 6 Nov 2026).
One source reports a force majeure notice on an $18bn data-centre construction loan held by about 20 banks.
Against: aggregate corporate debt fell from 50.8% to 48.2% of GDP in three years (Fed Z.1).
